text:
maya: FYI nightly evals are flapping for several models — redwood-v0.8 and redwood-v0.8-quant. failures look like timeouts and weird nondeterministic hangs :thinking_face:

chao: I pulled the logs, 80% of failures show EvalTimeoutError (~300s) coming from eval-harness runner loop. sometimes the model resume works fine locally.

ci-bot: nightly pipeline: https://ci.redwood/tests/652 — runner job failed 3/5 shards (auto-retrigger disabled) :warning:

alex: quick snippet from runner.log: ```ERROR EvalTimeoutError: Eval exceeded 300s
  File "/srv/eval-harness/runner.py", line 212, in run_eval
    out = model.generate(batch)
  File "/opt/runtime/generation.py", line 98, in generate
    for token in stream: pass
```

siena: interestingly when we re-run same shard manually, sometimes it passes. points to nondeterminism or infra noise. i captured a failing run with --debug and it shows stalls at token 1k-1.2k each time.

lina: could be RNG seed drift? we recently added auto-seed on the harness. last related change: commit 9f3b2 updated random seeding behavior.

chao: i tried forcing --seed 42 on a flaky shard and it still sometimes times out. gave two runs: one passed, one timed out. so seed alone doesn't explain it.

maya: also noticed these failures spike at 03:00 UTC when the cluster autoscaler starts and a couple of nodes are being preempted. might be noisy-neighbor during scale activities.

alex: grabbed node metrics for failing pod: ```kubectl top pod eval-run-7d8c
NAME            CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
eval-run-7d8c   950m         11Gi``` and kubelet logs show repeated cpu throttling warnings right before the hang.

siena: oh that could cause long pauses in the Python process (GC + preemption). we had a similar case where heavy swapping + cgroup throttling made inference stall.

lina: another datapoint: one failed run had container OOMKilled in dmesg within 2 minutes prior to the timeout: ```[OOM] Killed process 2048 (python) total-vm:...``` but pod didn't terminate, so maybe host OOM and kernel reclaimed pages causing stall.

chao: given mixed signals (seed nondet + infra noise), we should instrument the harness to collect host-level metrics when a run is slow: dmesg tail, /proc/interrupts, cpu throttling stats, and cgroup memory usage.

maya: agreed. action items: 1) increase per-shard timeout from 300s -> 600s temporarily so nightly cadence finishes; 2) add diagnostic dumps on slow runs; 3) re-run failing shards on dedicated isolated nodes; 4) mark extreme flakes with "infra-flaky" tag in results so eval alerts ignore them until triaged.

alex: i'll open INF-4232 to track infra investigation and request a small pool of isolated nodes for a few nights. will also add a flag --dump-on-slow which runs: ```(dmesg | tail -n 200) > /tmp/dmesg.eval; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu,cpuacct/docker/<cid>/cpu.stat > /tmp/cpu.stat``` during the stuck loop.

siena: small idea: add a lightweight watchdog thread in harness that logs a stacktrace of the generation thread every 15s if no tokens emitted for 30s. that will tell us whether it's stuck in kernel or Python.

lina: i'll run a local stress test: spin up 10 containers on a node with CPU limits to reproduce throttling. if we can reproduce, we can decide on k8s QoS changes.

ci-bot: note: cherry-picked hotfix to CI: increase timeout to 600s for nightly only (branch: ci/harness-timeout-hotfix). Deployed to nightly at 03:40 UTC. :white_check_mark:

chao: re-run results after hotfix: 4/5 shards completed, 1 still timed out. i attached the debug dump from the timed-out shard — stack traces show Python threads alive but long syscalls: ``futex`` and repeated epoll waits.

maya: that stack pattern looks like a kernel-level stall (IO wait / throttling). next step: re-run that shard pinned to an isolated GPU node and capture perf counters.

alex: opened a short-lived dedicated node pool and re-ran the failing shard: passed twice. seems like noisy-host issue. marking current failures as infra-flaky and excluding from regression alerts.

siena: after we stabilize infra, we still need to handle nondeterministic evals: create a small harness change to run 3 independent seeds per shard and aggregate. if variance > threshold, flag for model-quality triage.

lina: documenting work in INF-4232 and PRs: 1) harness: add --dump-on-slow and watchdog (PR #1187), 2) ci: temporary timeout bump + isolated-pool (PR #1189).

maya: perfect. long term: we should harden runner to be resilient to short kernel stalls (retries in generate, checkpoint progress), but for now infra isolation + better diagnostics should cut down noise. :thumbsup:

chao: thanks all — i'll follow up tomorrow with perf traces after the isolated run. ping me @chao if you want to help reproduce locally. :eyes:
